 Uruguay vs. Dominican Republic - Head-to-head record
 Uruguay and the Dominican Republic have met only once before , making this a relatively unfamiliar fixture in international football.
 Their previous encounter took place in October 2025, when Uruguay secured a narrow 1-0 victory in a friendly. That result gives the South American side a perfect head-to-head record, although one match offers limited evidence of how Tuesday’s contest might unfold.
 Uruguay will be looking to extend their advantage in front of their home supporters, while the Dominican Republic will hope to produce a more competitive performance and secure their first positive result against the Celeste.

 Uruguay – Celeste Chasing a Fourth Consecutive Victory
 Uruguay have enjoyed a strong run of results under interim manager Diego Forlán and will be looking to finish 2026 with another victory. Let’s examine their recent performances and expected line-up for this friendly.
 Recent form
 Uruguay have won their last three international friendlies, responding impressively after a disappointing World Cup campaign and a 3-1 defeat to Japan in September. The Celeste followed that setback with a 4-1 victory over South Korea and a commanding 6-1 win against India.
 Their winning streak continued on Friday, when Uruguay secured a 2-1 victory over Argentina at La Bombonera. That result provided another encouraging sign for Forlán, who has overseen a significant improvement in the team’s performances since taking temporary charge.
 Uruguay have scored 12 goals across their last three matches, demonstrating their attacking potential against different levels of opposition. However, Forlán is expected to use Tuesday’s friendly to assess other squad members rather than retain the side that defeated Argentina.
 The manager is preparing extensive changes, with Rodrigo Bentancur and Agustín Canobbio expected to be the only players keeping their places in the starting XI. Federico Valverde is set to begin on the bench again, while Federico Viñas and Rodrigo Aguirre could lead the attack. Santiago Mele is expected to start in goal.

 Dominican Republic – Caribbean Side Facing a Major Test
 The Dominican Republic have shown encouraging signs in recent months, particularly in the CONCACAF Nations League. However, facing Uruguay away from home represents a significant challenge for Marcelo Neveleff’s side.
 Recent form
 The Dominican Republic have recorded three victories in their last four CONCACAF Nations League matches, demonstrating an ability to compete against regional opponents. They began that sequence with a 3-2 home win over Nicaragua before securing a 2-1 away victory against Trinidad and Tobago.
 However, their defensive vulnerabilities were exposed in a 4-1 home defeat to Haiti . Neveleff’s side responded with a 2-1 victory away to Nicaragua in October, but their performances have remained inconsistent, particularly against stronger opposition.
 Their only friendly international of 2026 also ended in defeat, with Panama securing a 4-2 victory in June. The Dominican Republic have conceded at least twice in three of their last five matches, raising concerns ahead of a meeting with a Uruguay side that has scored freely in recent weeks.
 Neveleff will have Luis Meneses and former Real Madrid forward Mariano Díaz available for this encounter, providing additional attacking options. However, Real Betis left-back Junior Firpo is unavailable through injury, leaving the visitors without an important defensive player.

 Predictions for Uruguay vs. Dominican Republic - Uruguay to dominate
 Uruguay arrive in excellent attacking form, having scored 12 goals in their last three matches. Over 2.5 total goals is therefore an appealing option against a Dominican Republic side that has struggled defensively.
 The visitors have conceded four goals against both Panama and Haiti in recent months, while Uruguay have demonstrated their ability to make fast starts. With the hosts expected to dominate possession, Uruguay to be leading at half-time is another market worth considering.
 Despite the anticipated changes to Uruguay’s starting XI, the difference in quality between the sides remains considerable. Our main prediction is Uruguay to win with a -2 handicap .
